style_when: scale is the story — a port, a refinery, a data centre hall, a rail yard, a skyline of cranes — and the reader needs to feel how big it is
prompt: Telephoto film still, 200mm long-lens compression stacking layers at a Mississippi data center site: a row of rebuilt airliner jet engines mounted as turbine gensets in long weathered-orange steel containers, parked on cracked asphalt in the power yard, commanding the right third of frame. Behind them a vast graphite-grey data hall of corrugated steel rises flat and compressed; one distant transmission pylon sits small in the stacked layers. Last low sun rakes hard from the left, long cast shadows across the yard, rim light on the engine cowlings, steel-blue dusk above. Crystal-clear air, deep industrial contrast, everything sharp. Extreme asymmetric composition, generous sky negative space. Fine film grain, no people, no logos.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, signage, logos
rationale: Scale is the story: eight 50-megawatt machines standing in for a utility, so telephoto compression stacks the improvised turbine row flat against the permanent data hall and shrinks the absent grid to a distant pylon. It is a real energy-infrastructure scene, not a metaphor, and it rotates the desk away from the recent cinematic and flatlay treatments.
cue: Eight retired jet engines now power xAI's Mississippi data center
subject: A row of rebuilt airliner jet engines mounted as turbine gensets in steel containers, powering a data center site
core_thesis: AI infrastructure is switching to improvised local generation — scavenged jet engines on a pad — because the grid cannot arrive in time, while nobody owns the power feed beneath the edge sites being handed to agents.
core_conflict: Grid interconnection speed versus data-center build speed: improvised combustion fills the gap, and a single permit challenge can silence the whole feed.
composition: Extreme asymmetry: the turbine row commands the right third, the compressed data hall stacked flat behind it, a distant pylon small in the telephoto layers, generous sky negative space left
